config.title: Build CRDT lite collaborative text prototype

intro.title: Build CRDT lite collaborative text prototype
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simplified collaborative text editor prototype using a CRDT (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Type) approach. You'll learn how to manage shared state across multiple users by implementing a basic last-writer-wins register to handle concurrent edits. The core programming concepts involve using JavaScript objects, arrays, and functions to track changes and merge updates. You'll work with fundamental JavaScript constructs like state variables, event handlers, and DOM manipulation to create a real-time editing interface. By the end, you'll have a working prototype that demonstrates how collaborative editing can function without complex conflict resolution.
intro.usecase: CRDTs power real-time collaborative editing in products like Google Docs, Figma, and Notion, where multiple users can edit the same document simultaneously without conflicts. As a developer, you'll implement similar patterns for collaborative text fields in dashboards, shared code editors, or multiplayer whiteboards. Understanding CRDT principles helps you build responsive, conflict-free collaborative interfaces that feel instant to users, which is essential for modern SaaS applications with real-time features.

objectives: Initialize a collaborative text state using a CRDT-inspired array structure
Implement a function to insert characters at specific positions in the shared text
Apply a merge operation to combine local and remote text changes without conflicts
Construct a basic UI that renders the collaborative text and accepts user input
Configure event handlers to capture text edits and trigger state updates
Integrate a simulated network layer to exchange text operations between clients
Manipulate the text state to resolve concurrent edits using logical timestamps

steps.title: Import required modules and functions
steps.instruction: Import the required modules and functions that will be used throughout the lesson. Import the 'useState' hook from React.
steps.hint: You'll need to import React and the useState hook to manage state in your component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React and useState are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main CRDT prototype function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'crdtPrototype' that will serve as the main entry point for the CRDT implementation. The function should return null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure to name it exactly 'crdtPrototype'.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the crdtPrototype function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'crdtPrototype' is created and returns null.
successCriteria: The function 'crdtPrototype' exists and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named 'crdtPrototype' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Check the name and return value.

steps.title: Initialize the document state array
steps.instruction: Inside your crdtPrototype function, initialize a state variable named 'documentState' using useState, setting its initial value to an empty array.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useState with [] as the initial value and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing a state array
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The crdtPrototype function will have a documentState variable initialized as an empty array, ready to store character objects.
successCriteria: The crdtPrototype function contains a useState call that initializes documentState as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState to initialize documentState as an empty array inside the crdtPrototype function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing the state. Inside crdtPrototype, use useState to create a documentState variable with an initial value of an empty array.

steps.title: Create the generatePosition function
steps.instruction: Inside your crdtPrototype function, create a function named generatePosition that takes two parameters: left and right.
steps.hint: Add a function declaration inside crdtPrototype. The function should be defined but doesn't need to return anything yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: The crdtPrototype function now contains a nested generatePosition function that accepts left and right parameters.
successCriteria: generatePosition function is defined inside crdtPrototype with parameters left and right
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure generatePosition is defined inside crdtPrototype and accepts two parameters named left and right.
steps.feedbackWrong: The generatePosition function needs to be created inside crdtPrototype with parameters left and right.

steps.title: Create the insertCharacter function
steps.instruction: Inside the crdtPrototype function, define a function named insertCharacter that takes two parameters: character and position.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should be defined inside crdtPrototype but before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The insertCharacter function is defined with the correct name and parameters, ready to implement character insertion logic in the next step.
successCriteria: The insertCharacter function is defined inside crdtPrototype with parameters character and position.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'insertCharacter' and takes two parameters: character and position.
steps.feedbackWrong: The insertCharacter function isn't properly defined. Check that it's inside crdtPrototype, has the correct name, and accepts two parameters.

steps.title: Create the deleteCharacter function
steps.instruction: Inside the crdtPrototype function, create a function named deleteCharacter that takes a position parameter and marks characters as deleted rather than removing them from the documentState array.
steps.hint: You can mark a character as deleted by setting a 'deleted' property to true on the character object at the given position in documentState.
steps.expectedOutcome: A deleteCharacter function is defined inside crdtPrototype that handles character deletion by marking them as deleted.
successCriteria: The deleteCharacter function is defined with a position parameter and marks the character at that position as deleted in documentState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the deleteCharacter function, but make sure it properly marks characters as deleted in the documentState array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The deleteCharacter function is not yet correctly implemented. Review how to mark characters as deleted in the documentState array.

steps.title: Initialize the UI state variables
steps.instruction: Inside the crdtPrototype function, initialize two state variables: one to hold the current document text (call it 'documentText') and another to hold the user's input (call it 'inputValue'). Initialize both with empty strings.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to create state variables. The pattern is: const [variableName, setVariableName] = useState(initialValue).
steps.expectedOutcome: The crdtPrototype function will have two state variables: documentText and inputValue, both initialized as empty strings.
successCriteria: The function contains two useState calls: one for documentText and one for inputValue, both initialized with empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both state variables: documentText and inputValue. Both should be initialized with empty strings using useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the crdtPrototype function, use useState to create two state variables: documentText and inputValue, both starting as empty strings.

steps.title: Create the basic UI structure
steps.instruction: Inside the crdtPrototype function's return statement, create a basic UI structure with a heading, a text input field, a display area for the document text, and buttons for inserting and deleting characters.
steps.hint: Return a div containing an h1, an input, a paragraph for displaying the document text, and two buttons. Use the state variables and handler functions you've already created.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function returns a structured UI with a heading, input field, text display area, and control buttons.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a div containing an h1, an input, a paragraph, and two buttons.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return statement includes all required elements: a heading, input, paragraph, and two buttons inside a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UI structure is incomplete. Check that you're returning a div with all the specified elements.

steps.title: Wire event handlers to UI elements
steps.instruction: Add an onChange event handler to the input field that calls handleInsert with the event's target value.
steps.hint: Use the onChange attribute on the input element and pass a function that extracts the value from the event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The input field will trigger handleInsert whenever its value changes, connecting user typing to the CRDT insert operation.
successCriteria: The input element has an onChange handler that calls handleInsert with the event's target value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onChange handler properly calls handleInsert with the event's target value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field needs an onChange handler that calls handleInsert with the event's target value. Check the syntax for event handlers in React.
